summary: Specifies NETBLT (NETwork BLock Transfer), a transport-level protocol for quickly moving large amounts of data between computers. It is reliable, flow controlled and aims for high throughput over many kinds of networks. It was experimental, not a standard, and some parts were unfinished. It revises RFC 969.

eli5.summary: Instead of carrying a pile of bricks one at a time, you move them in big, checked batches. This protocol sends data in large blocks to go faster.

questions: how does bulk data transfer protocol work
